notes.A1: The left-bend stem and lower line direction match the neutral description; the warning identifies bend direction, not a new speed limit or priority rule.
notes.A2: Two bends are visible and the first turns left; the plural-bend meaning differs from the purpose/loading/draught-animal alternatives.
notes.A3: The drawn slope falls to the right; 10% is gradient, so the descent answer is unique and the distance/tunnel/zone alternatives do not fit.
notes.A4: The rising slope and percentage identify ascent; stop/continuous-line/parking-disc meanings do not describe this warning.
notes.A5: Both black edges bend inward, preserving the both-sides variant; narrowing does not assign priority to either direction.
notes.A6: The raised diagonal span over water identifies an opening bridge; retained wording does not confuse it with the road-ending-at-water warning.
notes.A7: The car approaches a water edge; wording describes the physical hazard without treating a barrier or a bridge opening as supplied facts.
notes.A8: Two surface humps depict unevenness; lower speed is appropriate advice rather than an invented numerical limit.
notes.A9: The single raised hump matches the selected variant; the family can also represent a dip, and the wording keeps that distinction.
notes.A10: The car and zigzag tracks support slippery surface; the explicit not-only-snow/ice boundary matches the Swedish source.
notes.A11: The wheel throws fragments; the source's ordinary gravel-road qualification is preserved rather than warning of falling rocks.
notes.A12: Fragments fall from the right-side face; the neutral description and mirrored-variant qualification agree with the illustration.
notes.A13: A pedestrian over stripes inside a warning triangle warns of a crossing ahead; it is not the crossing's own priority/control instruction.
notes.A14: An adult with a child matches the warning's pedestrian-presence scope; no compulsory-path meaning or numeric speed is added.
notes.A15: The two children support the children-ahead meaning; the warning supplies no numerical speed limit.
notes.A16: The cyclist pictogram warns of cyclists/moped riders crossing or entering; it does not prescribe a cycle-only route.
notes.A17: Skis and poles identify the crossing/presence hazard, distinct from a ski-service or chair-lift destination symbol.
notes.A18: The mounted horse faces left and matches the physical description; this is rider warning, not a prohibition on riding.
notes.A19: The selected silhouette is a moose; generic animal-warning wording correctly permits other official animal symbols.
notes.A20: The digging worker represents works along the road, without guessing an exact temporary traffic arrangement.
notes.A21: The crossed digging-worker panel ends the A20-marked section; unrelated restrictions do not automatically expire.
notes.A22: The three lamps are red/yellow/green; the warning anticipates a signal and does not grant permission to proceed.
notes.A23: The aircraft's nose points left in this asset; opposite-facing official variants retain the same low-aircraft warning meaning.
notes.A24: The windsock extends left; crosswind wording is site-adapted and does not claim a numerical wind threshold.
notes.A25: The opposed vertical arrows and source specify transition from a one-way carriageway to two-way traffic, not general priority.
